conventions.convention: The alphabet is finite and nonempty, n starts at 1, and the reference probability p has strictly positive mass at every letter. The simplex carries d₁(q,r)=Σa|q(a)−r(a)|.
Relative entropy uses natural logarithms and omits zero-mass terms. The constrained entropy is s(u)=−min{D(q∥p):h(q)=u}; canonical weights contain exp(−nβh).

The LDP uses speed n, open-set lower bounds and closed-set upper bounds, with inf ∅=+∞ and ln 0=−∞. The space is nonempty compact metric, I is lower semicontinuous and not identically infinite, and F is continuous and real-valued.

Microcanonical shells use the strict inequality |h(L_n)−u|<δ. The asserted iterated shell limit requires a sequence δ_j decreasing to zero with equal open-shell and closed-shell entropy infima. Conditional laws require positive shell probability.
An upper supporting line at u has slope β and must satisfy s(v)≤s(u)+β(v−u) throughout the whole energy range; canonical realization concerns variational equilibrium energies.
The Curie–Weiss model is dimensionless, with uniform binary reference law, J>0, β≥0, magnetization m=q(+1)−q(−1), and energy h=−Jm²/2.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite nonempty alphabet, full-support reference probability p and continuous h on the probability simplex, the canonical macrostate law has speed-n LDP rate Rβ(q)=D(q∥p)+βh(q)−min_r[D(r∥p)+βh(r)]. Under the stated matching-shell hypothesis the iterated shell logarithmic limit is s(u), and the conditioned macrostates concentrate near M_u. Moreover h(Mβ)=argmax_v[s(v)−βv], and u is a canonical energy at β exactly when s(v)≤s(u)+β(v−u) on the whole energy range.

For the stated speed-n LDP on a nonempty compact metric space with lower semicontinuous I:K→[0,+∞] not identically infinite and continuous F:K→R, n⁻¹ ln Z_n converges to c=sup_K(F−I), and the normalized exponential tilt satisfies an LDP with good rate I_F=I−F+c. Its zero set is precisely argmax_K(F−I).

Defines finite product reference laws, empirical probability vectors, normalized canonical weights proportional to p^{⊗n}exp(−nβh(L_n)), constrained costs d(u), entropy s(u)=−d(u), canonical and constrained variational sets, and positive-probability microcanonical shell conditioning.
